lesson.title: Centre, radius, diameter
lesson.body: Every point on a circle is the same distance from its centre. That distance is the radius. A diameter goes across through the centre, so it is two radii.

lesson.title: Chord and circumference
lesson.body: A chord joins two points on the circle; the diameter is the longest chord. The circumference is the distance all the way around.

lesson.title: π
lesson.body: For every circle, circumference ÷ diameter is the same number, π: a little more than 3. We use 3.14 or 22/7 for it, or leave the answer in terms of π.

lesson.title: The formula
lesson.body: Circumference = π × diameter = 2 × π × radius. Read which one the question gives you.

lesson.title: Why π × r × r
lesson.body: Cut a circle into thin slices and lay them head to tail: they make nearly a rectangle, half the circumference long (π × r) and one radius high. Area = π × r × r.

lesson.title: Radius, not diameter
lesson.body: Given the diameter, halve it first: a circle 10 cm across has r = 5, and its area is π × 25 = 25π cm².

lesson.title: Parts of circles
lesson.body: A semicircle is half a circle: half the area. Split a figure into squares, rectangles and circle parts, and add or take away.

lesson.title: Curved edges
lesson.body: A track's two semicircular ends make one whole circle, so one lap is 2 × the straight + π × the diameter.

templates.construct: Find the diameter from the radius

formats.prompt: A circle has a radius of {r} cm. What is its diameter?
The radius of a plate is {r} cm. How wide is the plate across its centre?

hints: The diameter goes across the circle through the centre.
That is two radii end to end.
templates.explain: The diameter is two radii: 2 × {r} = {answer} cm.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm halves the radius. The diameter is twice the radius.
{value} cm is the radius. The diameter is twice as long.

templates.construct: Find the radius from the diameter

formats.prompt: A circle has a diameter of {d} cm. What is its radius?
A round clock face is {d} cm across. How far is it from the centre to the edge?

hints: The radius goes from the centre to the edge.
It is half of the diameter.
templates.explain: The radius is half the diameter: {d} ÷ 2 = {answer} cm.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm doubles the diameter. The radius is half of it.
{value} cm is the diameter. The radius is half.

templates.construct: Find a circumference in terms of π

formats.prompt: A circle has a diameter of {d} cm. What is its circumference, in terms of π?

hints: Circumference = π × diameter.
The diameter is {d} cm.

distractors.feedback: {value}π doubles the diameter. 2 × π × r uses the radius; with the diameter it is just π × {d}.
{value}π is the area, π × r × r. The circumference is π × diameter.
{value}π uses the radius. Circumference = π × diameter, or 2 × π × radius.

formats.prompt: Use π = 3.14. A circle has a radius of {r} cm. What is its circumference?
Use π = 3.14. A round garden has a radius of {r} m. How many metres of fence go around it?

hints: Circumference = 2 × π × radius.
2 × {r} = {2 * r}, the diameter.

distractors.feedback: {value} uses the radius as the diameter. Circumference = π × diameter = 3.14 × {2 * r}.
{value} is the area, π × r × r. The circumference is 2 × π × r.

templates.construct: Find how far a wheel rolls in one turn, with π = 22/7

formats.prompt: Use π = 22/7. A wheel has a diameter of {d} cm. How far does it roll in one full turn?
Use π = 22/7. The wheel of a wheelbarrow is {d} cm across. How far does the wheelbarrow move when the wheel turns once?

hints: In one turn, a wheel rolls its circumference.
Circumference = π × diameter = 22/7 × {d}.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm doubles the diameter. With the diameter, C = π × d = 22/7 × {d}.
{value} cm is the diameter. One turn rolls the circumference, π × {d}.

templates.construct: Find the area of a circle in terms of π from its radius

formats.prompt: A circle has a radius of {r} cm. What is its area, in terms of π?

hints: Area = π × radius × radius.
So the area is {r * r} lots of π.

distractors.feedback: {value}π is the circumference, 2 × π × r. Area is π × r × r.
{value}π uses the diameter, {2 * r}, as the radius. Use r = {r}.

templates.construct: Find the area of a circle in terms of π from its diameter

formats.prompt: A circle has a diameter of {d} cm. What is its area, in terms of π?

hints: Find the radius first: half of the diameter.

distractors.feedback: {value}π squares the diameter. Halve it first: r = {r}.
{value}π is the circumference, π × d. Area is π × r × r.

templates.construct: Find the area of a circle with π = 3.14

formats.prompt: Use π = 3.14. A circle has a radius of {r} cm. What is its area?
Use π = 3.14. A round rug has a radius of {r} dm. What is its area in square decimetres?

hints: Area = π × r × r.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the circumference, 2 × π × r. Area is π × r × r.
{value} uses the diameter as the radius. Use r = {r}.

templates.construct: Find the area of a semicircle with π = 3.14

formats.prompt: Use π = 3.14. A semicircle has a diameter of {d} cm. What is its area?
Use π = 3.14. A half-moon window is a semicircle {d} cm across. What is its area?

hints: A semicircle is half a circle: find the circle's area, then halve it.
r = {d} ÷ 2 = {r}, so the circle is 3.14 × {r * r} = {3.14 * r * r}.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm² is the whole circle. A semicircle is half.
{value} cm² uses the diameter as the radius. Halve it first: r = {r}.

templates.construct: Find the area of a square with a semicircle on top, with π = 3.14

formats.prompt: Use π = 3.14. A window is a square {s} cm wide with a semicircle on top. The semicircle's diameter is the square's top side. What is the area of the window?

hints: Add the square and the semicircle.
Square: {s} × {s} = {s * s}. Semicircle: half of 3.14 × {r} × {r}.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm² adds a whole circle. The top is only a semicircle: halve it.
{value} cm² is only the square. Add the semicircle on top.

templates.construct: Find the distance around a running track: two straights and two semicircles

formats.prompt: Use π = 3.14. A running track has two straight sides, each {L} m long, joined by two semicircles with a diameter of {d} m. How long is one lap?

hints: One lap is the two straights and the two semicircles.
Two semicircles make one whole circle: 3.14 × {d} = {3.14 * d}.

distractors.feedback: {value} m counts two whole circles. Two semicircles make just one.
{value} m is only the straights. Add the curved ends.

templates.construct: Find how far a wheel travels in a number of turns, with π = 22/7

formats.prompt: Use π = 22/7. A bicycle wheel has a diameter of 70 cm. How many metres does the bicycle go when the wheel turns {n} times?

hints: One turn rolls the circumference: 22/7 × 70.
{n} × 220 cm = {220 * n} cm. Change it to metres.

distractors.feedback: {value} is in centimetres. The question asks for metres: ÷ 100.
{value} m uses the diameter. One turn rolls the circumference, 220 cm.

templates.construct: Find the area of a ring in terms of π

formats.prompt: A ring is the space between two circles with the same centre, of radius {R} cm and {r} cm. What is its area, in terms of π?
A round pond has a radius of {r} m, and a path goes around it out to a radius of {R} m. What is the area of the path, in terms of π?

hints: Take the small circle away from the big one.
Big: π × {R} × {R} = {R * R}π. Small: π × {r} × {r} = {r * r}π.
{R * R}π − {r * r}π = ?π

distractors.feedback: {value}π squares the width of the ring, {R} − {r}. Take the small circle's area from the big one's.
{value}π adds the two circles. The ring is the big one with the small one taken out.

templates.construct: Find a circumference with π = 3.14, ignoring a height

formats.prompt: A round table is {d} cm across and stands {h} cm tall. Using π = 3.14, how far is it around the edge of the table?

hints: The distance round a circle is its circumference: π × diameter.
The height of the table is not needed.
templates.explain: 3.14 × {d} = {answer} cm. The height of the table was extra information.

distractors.feedback: {value} cm uses the height. The distance round the edge needs the diameter, {d} cm.
{value} cm is 2 × π × {d}, as if {d} cm were the radius. {d} cm across is the diameter.

templates.construct: Find pi as the circumference over the diameter, from measurements

formats.prompt: Ana wraps a string round a plate: it is {c} cm long. The plate is {d} cm across. Divide the distance round by the distance across. What do you get, to the nearest hundredth?
The distance round a can is {c} cm, and the can is {d} cm across. What is the distance round divided by the distance across, to the nearest hundredth?

hints: Divide the circumference by the diameter.
Round to two places after the point.
templates.explain: {c} ÷ {d} is about {answer}. For any circle this comes out close to 3.14: the number we call π.

distractors.feedback: {value} is the distance across divided by the distance round. Divide the circumference by the diameter: {c} ÷ {d}.
{value} is {c} − {d}. The question asks how many times the diameter fits round: divide.

templates.construct: See why a circle's area is pi times r times r, by cutting it into slices

formats.prompt: A circle with a radius of {r} cm is cut into many equal slices. The slices are laid side by side, points up and points down, to make a shape very close to a parallelogram. Its height is the radius, and its base is half the circumference. With π = 22/7, how long is the base?

hints: The whole circumference is 2 × π × r.
Half of it is π × r.
templates.explain: The base is half the circumference, π × {r} = {answer} cm. So the area is base × height = π × r × r: {answer} × {r} = {answer * r} cm².

distractors.feedback: {value} cm is the whole circumference. The slices pointing up make half of it, and the ones pointing down the other half.
{value} cm is the radius, which is the height of the shape. The base is half the circumference.
